A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ConSim and contain matching framework definitions and experiments. The text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulatability experiments across four classification datasets, including method rankings and statistical comparisons using GPT-4o-mini and Gemini simulators.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds NoProjection comparisons, correlations with other evaluation metrics, and distributions of simulatability scores.

M1.justification: The three-phase ConSim procedure, CMAW and o1CA interpretation methods, Gradient Input importance, concept filtering, and Copeland aggregation remain unchanged. NoProjection enters as an evaluated comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BIOS10, IMDB, Rotten Tomatoes, and Tweet Eval Emotion. The classification tasks and scenarios using real or anonymized class labels are retained; the added analyses introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds NoProjection throughout the main and cross-simulator comparisons, providing a substantive control for whether concept extraction improves on explaining existing neurons directly. All five original extraction methods remain. The original no-explanation baseline is renamed NoExplanation.

E3.justification: v4 introduces comparison against eleven faithfulness and complexity metrics and newly reports testing alternative importance encodings. The existing model configurations, concept-count search, and 20-learning/20-evaluation sample protocol remain. Section 5.1 changes the experiment total from 23,360 to 24,560, although Appendix B.1 retains the earlier total.

E4.justification: New analyses examine simulatability's relationship to other metrics (Figure 5) and expose score distributions by dataset, extraction method, and prompt type (Figure 8). Appendix B.3 also newly reports that symbolic importance encodings outperformed numerical and verbal alternatives. The original prompt ablations remain.

E5.justification: Figure 5 introduces Spearman rank-correlation estimation. Existing statistical practices remain: five evaluation seeds, two additional validation sets, pairwise mean differences and standard deviations, and Student's tests with a 0.05 threshold. No increase in repeated-run counts is documented.

E6.justification: NoProjection results substantially expand the comparisons: in Table 2's DistilBERT+ row, it ranks first and NMF moves from first to second in the expanded field. Figure 5 adds correlations including -0.620 for activated-concept fraction and 0.459 for logits KL. Shared GPT-4o-mini pairwise values largely remain unchanged; these additions do not establish improved performance of the retained methods.

T1.justification: Figure 2 corrects the composition for concept embeddings from h composed with t to t composed with h, including the corresponding word-selection expression, resolving an inconsistency with Section 3. The main formalization and Equations 1–10 remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim that simulatability evaluates both faithfulness and plausibility with evaluation of explanation usefulness. The later discussion proposes a trade-off between faithfulness and complexity. The abstract's central contribution, consistent-ranking claim, and overall NMF recommendation remain.

C2.justification: The expanded Take-away section attributes NMF/SAE performance to positive, sparse representations, identifies concept interpretation as a bottleneck, and discusses uncertainty about which explanation property different simulators measure. The metric analysis adds a faithfulness–complexity interpretation. The original limitations concerning human validation, outdated SAEs, and layer selection remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds a worked BIOS10/T5+/NMF prompt and response example, explicitly shortened for display rather than changing the experimental sample count. Appendix D documents metric calculations, and the code link changes from an anonymous to an author-named GitHub repository. Existing model and SAE implementation settings remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds explicit positioning against ALMANACS, counterfactual simulatability, and FRAME, plus further support for LLM-based evaluation. Additional citations support NoProjection and the metric analysis. The claim of applying simulatability specifically to concept-based explanations is retained.

P1.justification: Selected introduction, background, and results paragraphs are rewritten. Conclusion becomes Take-away with Summary, Recommendations, and Discussions; the experiment-settings and supplementary-visualization appendices exchange positions. Most of the main section sequence and methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the metric-correlation chart and four-panel score-distribution figure, expands comparison tables and matrices for NoProjection, and adds boxed prompt examples. Figure 2's labels and compositions are corrected, matrix axes are revised, and existing appendix displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: The NoProjection control addresses a missing comparison with raw-neuron explanations, while metric analyses and worked prompts make the evaluation more informative and reproducible. Benefits are tempered by inconsistent experiment totals in Section 5.1 versus Appendix B.1 and NoProjection/SAE rankings in Table 3 that disagree with Figures 9–10. These gains support a modest overall improvement, while the acknowledged uncertainty about agreement with human rankings remains.
